incident-bot: [INCIDENT][P0] GPU OOM spike observed in decode-pool-usw2-3 during streaming decode. Error rate jumped at ~2025-11-12T14:12:39Z. Pager -> @sarah. Preliminary impact: ~5% request drops, some partial streams. Auto-fallback to rw/gptx-small-quant triggered but drops continued.

sarah: ack, i'm oncall, pulling logs and checking pool health.

sarah: running node check: `rctl cluster nodes --pool decode-pool-usw2` - several nodes reporting GPU memory pressure/oom markers.

anita: infra here — host g-decode-07 is in a restart loop, kernel shows CUDA ERROR 2 and process-level OOM during decode.
matt: runtime — could be runaway generation. any recent changes to SDK or gateway that affect max_tokens handling?
eli: support — CS getting tickets: customers report truncated streams and connection drops. Ticket IDs: #98723, #98724. High-volume customer noticed ~15% failures.
sarah: grabbing a sample request id for rootcause: req_0a1b2c. pulling logs now.

sarah: log excerpt for req_0a1b2c:
```
[2025-11-12T14:13:02Z] ERROR decode: cuda::alloc failed: out of memory
stack: decode_loop.cpp:423 run_batch -> kv_cache.cpp:87
request_id=req_0a1b2c model=rw/gptx-003 sequence_len=4096 tokens_generated=32768 user_max_tokens=0
headers: {"x-max-tokens": null, "client-retry": "false"}
```

matt: that header looks like user_max_tokens=0 / null. our runtime falls back to model default when header missing which in some prompt loops can lead to unbounded generation. that explains tokens_generated=32768.
anita: host metrics: g-decode-07 GPU mem 98%, committed pages start swapping, container restarts every ~20s.
sarah: mitigation plan: 
1) throttle/de-prioritize streaming decode traffic into decode-pool-usw2 (apply rate-limit at gateway)
2) hotpatch gateway to enforce per-request token cap (server-side default)
3) shift traffic away from affected nodes/pool to smaller-variant pool (rw/gptx-small-quant) or CPU fallback
4) drain and restart unhealthy nodes after traffic shift

eli: can we do a fast config change to enforce header-based cap? customers are still impacted.
matt: yes. i'm going to push gateway hotpatch: set `route.decode.enforce_max_tokens=true` and `route.decode.default_max_tokens=2048`. rollout 5% -> 100% (should be quick).

incident-bot: config-rollout started by matt at 1758009999, link: https://console/redwood/configs/rollout/abcd

sarah: monitoring metrics after patch (t+2m):
```
pre-patch: decode_pool_errors: 520/min, request_drops: 3.9%
post-patch(2m): decode_pool_errors: 120/min, request_drops: 0.9%
```
anita: draining g-decode-07 now: `kubectl drain g-decode-07 --ignore-daemonsets` then restarting inference service: `systemctl restart redwood-inference` on the node.
sarah: node restart done, GPU mem stable on that host. reclaiming capacity.
eli: customer impact summary draft: affected ~7 orgs, 2 enterprise tenants saw ~10-15% failures for ~8-12 minutes during spike. i'll post updates to tickets and send templated CS note.
matt: follow-up engineering work: add a runtime hard-cap guard that will clamp generated tokens to 16384 and circuit-break on kv-cache growth > threshold. also add telemetry to surface requests with missing max_tokens header.
anita: infra will add a NaN/zero check at ingress to reject headers with invalid token caps. also adding node-level oom alerting to catch earlier.
sarah: plan for handover: i'll remain primary for 30m to watch metrics and then hand to matt for follow-up. @matt you'll take ownership of the post-incident RCA and mitigation tickets.
matt: ack. i'll open a follow-up doc and assign tasks: runtime-guard, gateway-default, infra-alerting.
anita: preliminary root cause: client / SDK allowed unset max_tokens; combined with certain prompts produced runaway generation which saturated GPU memory and triggered CUDA OOMs and container restarts leading to request drops.
eli: CS continuity: preparing a one-pager with affected timestamps, tenants, and mitigation steps for compliance.
sarah: marking incident as resolved -> monitoring. will file incident report with timeline and action items. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 2025-11-12T14:40:55Z. Duration: ~28m. Final metrics: peak errors 560/min, total affected requests ~14k, layered mitigations: gateway cap + node restart + traffic shift. Postmortem owner: matt.

sarah: closing thread. follow-ups will be tracked in docs/eng/incidents/1758009999-rca.md
